title: Filtering the employees table by numbers · part 3

steps.title: Keep salary != 5200.0
steps.prompt:
Numbers compare with small symbols:
  > bigger   < smaller   = exactly   != not equal
Keep the rows where salary is not equal to 5200.0.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary != 5200.0;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM employees.
Add WHERE after the table name.
The test is salary != 5200.0.
Write: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary != 5200.0;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary != 5200.0;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE keeps only the rows that pass the test.

steps.title: Count rows salary != 5200.0
steps.prompt: COUNT(*) counts how many rows survive the filter.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT count(*) FROM employees WHERE salary != 5200.0;
hints: Start with SELECT count(*).
FROM employees.
Add WHERE salary != 5200.0.
Write: SELECT count(*) FROM employees WHERE salary != 5200.0;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM employees WHERE salary != 5200.0;
steps.memory_trick: count(*) + WHERE = 'how many pass?'

steps.title: Filter then sort: salary != 5200.0
steps.prompt:
Filter first, then ORDER BY tidies what is left.
LIMIT 3 keeps the top of that sorted list.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary != 5200.0 ORDER BY salary LIMIT 3;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM employees.
Add WHERE salary != 5200.0.
Add ORDER BY salary LIMIT 3.
Write: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary != 5200.0 ORDER BY salary LIMIT 3;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary != 5200.0 ORDER BY salary LIMIT 3;
